summary: Enumerated all ES solutions for primes p<=3000 (divisor method, validated against the f4 U-data for n<3000) and recorded the Legendre pattern of (x,y,z) mod l, l=3,5,7, for denominators prime to l. Every locally allowed unordered pattern (from 4uvw = p(uv+vw+wu) mod l) occurs globally (l=3: 2/2 patterns, l=5: 4/4, l=7: 4/4), so no hidden sign constraint shows up at these moduli. Caveat: patterns are sorted, so ordering information is discarded.
Closure check is trivial: i*i = -1, so the N-span of 1,i,j,k is not multiplicatively closed. The cone-design question has no ES-specific content beyond this basic fact.

Closure check by hand: (eps+i)^2 = eps^2-1+2 eps i has Re<0 for 0<eps<1, so the closed first quadrant {Re>0, Im>=0} is not multiplicatively closed (PROVED). The cone question was settled by H00's Z0067 search for the closed-Q1 cone, which contains ES exactly as its real slice.

The case y=z is symmetric.

For u = -omega^2 one has u^2 = u - 1, so the semiring N[1,u] is not multiplicatively closed (PROVED). The first step (test closure of candidate cones) rules this cone out; other small unit cones were not enumerated.

The statement as written is false: for every prime p=3 mod 4 the curve y^2=x^3-x has a_p=0 (checked to 1200), so a_p mod 8 cannot equal (2/p) = +-1. The correct form holds in range: for p=1 mod 4 (95 primes below 1200), a_p/2 mod 4 equals (2/p) mapped to 1 or 3 in all 95 cases. Sanity check only.

rho(residual log U, tau((p+3)/4)) = +0.62 for p=1 mod 4 up to 3e4 (raw 0.51). The first three x-values (x - ceil(p/4) <= 2) carry on average only 46% of solutions (median 45%, n=211 primes below 3000), so U is not concentrated at the first few x.

U mod 6 among p=1 mod 4 up to 3e4 (1600 primes): residues 0..5 at 0.161, 0.150, 0.163, 0.183, 0.168, 0.176. Bias at U=1 mod 6 is -1.8 SE. Repeated denominators do not occur for p=1 mod 4 (Z0259 lemma), so the separation step is moot.
